title: Euler's totient theorem over the constructed integers (Int.euler_totient_theorem)
statement: Euler's totient theorem, over the constructed integers: for every n : Nat with 0 < n and every a : Int coprime to n, a raised to the totient of n is congruent to 1 modulo n. The totient is NOT imported or axiomatised -- it is this kernel's own `AxNat.countRange (fun k => AxNat.beq (AxNat.gcd k n) 1) n`, the count of k in [0,n) coprime to n, so the statement is self-contained in the constructed naturals and integers. (At n = 1 that count is 1, since gcd(0,1) = 1; at n > 1 the k = 0 term is excluded because gcd(0,n) = n.) Established here rather than imported: `proof_route` is `kernel-lean` and `Kernel::axiom_footprint` for this declaration is EMPTY, measured by `theorem_axiom_footprint` as `integer Int.euler_totient_theorem 0`, in a prelude whose 1054 theorems are all axiom-free with 0 trusted declarations. What this does NOT claim: no statement about efficiency, no decision procedure, and no converse -- the hypothesis 0 < n and the coprimality hypothesis are both load-bearing and neither is discharged here.

formal.statement: theorem Int.euler_totient_theorem : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : Int) -> ((x2 : AxNat.lt AxNat.zero x0) -> ((x3 : Int.Coprime x1 (Int.ofNat x0)) -> Int.ModEq (Int.ofNat x0) (Int.pow x1 (AxNat.countRange (fun (x4 : AxNat) => AxNat.beq (AxNat.gcd x4 x0) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0)) Int.one))))
